Incorrect. Security through obscurity relies on hiding how a system works. Hilda's design openly separates privileges between roles, so it has nothing to do with secrecy.

questions.stem: Patrick was asked to implement a threat-hunting program for his organization. Which one of the following is the basic assumption of a threat-hunting program that he should use as he plans his work?
options: Security controls were designed using a defense-in-depth strategy.
Attackers may already be present on the network.
Defense mechanisms may contain unpatched vulnerabilities.
questions.explanation: While all of these assumptions are valid premises that Patrick might have going into the exercise, the basic assumption of a threat-hunting exercise is the so-called presumption of compromise. This means that Patrick should assume that attackers have already gained access to his system and then hunt for indicators of their presence.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Defense in depth is a valid control-design premise for layering imperfect controls, but it is not the core premise of threat hunting. Hunting assumes the controls may already have failed.
Incorrect. Audits that find control deficiencies are part of assessment and compliance work. Threat hunting goes further and assumes an attacker is already inside, then searches for signs of them.
Correct. Threat hunting starts from the presumption of compromise: it assumes attackers already have access and then searches for indicators that they are present.
Incorrect. Unpatched vulnerabilities are the concern of vulnerability and patch management programs. That assumption may be true, but it is not the basic premise of threat hunting.

questions.stem: Brian is developing the training program for his organization's disaster recovery program and would like to make sure that participants understand when disaster activity concludes. Which one of the following events marks the completion of a disaster recovery process?
options: Restoring operations in an alternate facility
Restoring operations in the primary facility
questions.explanation: The end goal of the disaster recovery process is restoring normal business operations in the primary facility. All of the other actions listed may take place during the disaster recovery process, but the process is not complete until the organization is once again functioning normally in its primary facilities.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Protecting life and property is the first priority after a disaster, but it happens at the start of the response. Recovery still has a long way to go after that.
Incorrect. Running from an alternate site is only a temporary arrangement during recovery. The DR process isn't finished until operations go back to the primary facility.
Correct. The goal of disaster recovery is getting normal business operations running again in the primary facility. The process is only complete when that happens.
Incorrect. First responders are stood down once the immediate emergency is under control, which happens early in the process. Restoration and the move back to the primary site still remain.

questions.stem: Melanie suspects that someone is using malicious software to steal computing cycles from her company. Which one of the following security tools would be in the best position to detect this type of incident?
questions.explanation: A host-based intrusion detection system (HIDS) may be able to detect unauthorized processes running on a system. The other controls mentioned, network intrusion detection systems (NIDSs), firewalls, and DLP systems, are network-based and may not notice rogue processes.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A NIDS watches network traffic. A cryptomining process using up CPU on a host may not show any clear sign on the network, so a NIDS is poorly placed to spot it.
Incorrect. A firewall allows or blocks traffic at network boundaries. It has no view of the processes running on a system, so it would not notice a rogue program using up computing cycles.
Correct. A HIDS runs on the host itself and watches local activity, so it can catch unauthorized processes, such as cryptomalware, that use up CPU cycles.

Incorrect. DLP looks for sensitive data leaving the organization. Stealing computing cycles doesn't involve moving data out, and the network-based DLP the book has in mind wouldn't see rogue processes.

questions.stem: Brandon observes that an authorized user of a system on his network recently misused his account to exploit a system vulnerability against a shared server that allowed him to gain root access to that server. What type of attack took place?
questions.explanation: The scenario describes a privilege escalation attack where a malicious insider with authorized access to a system misused that access to gain privileged credentials.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A denial-of-service attack tries to make a system or service unavailable. Here the user did not disrupt the server; he exploited a vulnerability to gain root access.
Correct. An authorized user misused his ordinary access and exploited a vulnerability to get root (privileged) rights on the server, which is a privilege escalation attack.

Incorrect. Reconnaissance means gathering information about targets, such as scanning or footprinting, before an attack. This user actually exploited a flaw and gained root, so the attack went past reconnaissance.
Incorrect. A brute-force attack guesses passwords repeatedly until one works. The user already had valid credentials and got root through a software vulnerability, not by guessing passwords.

questions.stem: Carla has worked for her company for 15 years and has held a variety of different positions. Each time she changed positions, she gained new privileges associated with that position, but no privileges were ever taken away. What concept describes the sets of privileges she has accumulated?
questions.explanation: Carla's account has experienced privilege creep, where privileges accumulated over time. This condition is also known as aggregation and likely constitutes a violation of the least privilege principle.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Entitlement means the privileges a user is granted when the account is provisioned. It says nothing about privileges piling up across role changes, so it doesn't describe Carla's situation.

Correct. Privilege creep (also called aggregation) is when privileges pile up over time because new ones are granted at each job change and old ones are never removed. This likely violates least privilege.
Incorrect. Transitivity describes trust that passes along a chain (if A trusts B and B trusts C, A may trust C). It is not about one user collecting privileges over time.
Incorrect. Isolation means keeping processes or systems separate so they can't interfere with each other. It has nothing to do with a user building up access rights across positions.

questions.stem: During what phase of the incident response process do administrators take action to limit the effect or scope of an incident?
questions.explanation: The mitigation phase of incident response focuses on actions that can contain the damage incurred during an incident. This includes limiting the scope and/or effectiveness of the incident. The detection phase identifies that an incident is taking place. The response phase includes steps taken to assemble a team and triage the incident. At the conclusion of the recovery phase, normal operations are resumed.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Detection is the phase where an incident is first identified as taking place. Nothing is done there to contain it or limit its scope.
Incorrect. The response phase is about assembling the incident response team and triaging the incident. Containing the damage comes in the next phase.
Correct. Mitigation is the phase that contains the damage from an incident, which means limiting its scope and/or its effectiveness.
Incorrect. Recovery is the phase that brings systems back to normal operations. It comes after the incident has already been contained.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Ann is a security professional for a midsize business and typically handles log analysis and security monitoring tasks for her organization. One of her roles is to monitor alerts originating from the organization's intrusion detection system. The system typically generates several dozen alerts each day, and many of those alerts turn out to be false alarms after her investigation. This morning, the intrusion detection system alerted because the network began to receive an unusually high volume of inbound traffic. Ann received this alert and began looking into the origin of the traffic.

At this point in the incident response process, what term best describes what has occurred in Ann's organization?
questions.explanation: At this point in the process, Ann has no reason to believe that any actual security compromise or policy violation took place, so this situation does not meet the criteria for a security incident or intrusion. Rather, the alert generated by the intrusion detection system is simply a security event requiring further investigation. Security occurrence is not a term commonly used in incident handling.
optionNotes: Incorrect. "Security occurrence" isn't a standard incident-handling term, so it can't be the best description of an IDS alert that is still being investigated.
Incorrect. An incident needs an actual compromise or policy violation. So far Ann has no evidence of either, so the alert doesn't yet count as an incident.
Correct. The IDS alert about unusual inbound traffic is an observable occurrence that still needs investigating. Nothing confirms a compromise yet, so it is a security event.
Incorrect. An intrusion means someone actually got unauthorized access to a system or network. Nothing at this stage shows that happened, so this term goes too far.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Ann is a security professional for a midsize business and typically handles log analysis and security monitoring tasks for her organization. One of her roles is to monitor alerts originating from the organization's intrusion detection system. The system typically generates several dozen alerts each day, and many of those alerts turn out to be false alarms after her investigation. This morning, the intrusion detection system alerted because the network began to receive an unusually high volume of inbound traffic. Ann received this alert and began looking into the origin of the traffic.

Ann continues her investigation and realizes that the traffic generating the alert is abnormally high volumes of inbound UDP traffic on port 53. What service typically uses this port?
questions.explanation: DNS traffic commonly uses port 53 for both TCP and UDP communications. SSH and SCP use TCP port 22. SSL and TLS do not have ports assigned to them but are commonly used for HTTPS traffic on port 443. Unencrypted web traffic over HTTP often uses port 80.
optionNotes: Correct. DNS uses port 53 over both UDP (standard queries) and TCP (zone transfers, large responses). A large flood of inbound UDP/53 traffic is typical of a DNS amplification attack.
Incorrect. SSH and SCP run over TCP port 22, not UDP port 53, so they don't account for this traffic.
Incorrect. SSL/TLS doesn't have its own assigned port. It usually secures HTTPS on TCP port 443, which doesn't match UDP 53.
Incorrect. Unencrypted HTTP web traffic usually uses TCP port 80, not UDP port 53.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Ann is a security professional for a midsize business and typically handles log analysis and security monitoring tasks for her organization. One of her roles is to monitor alerts originating from the organization's intrusion detection system. The system typically generates several dozen alerts each day, and many of those alerts turn out to be false alarms after her investigation. This morning, the intrusion detection system alerted because the network began to receive an unusually high volume of inbound traffic. Ann received this alert and began looking into the origin of the traffic.

As Ann analyzes the traffic further, she realizes that the traffic is coming from many different sources and has overwhelmed the network, preventing legitimate uses. The inbound packets are responses to queries that she does not see in outbound traffic. The responses are abnormally large for their type. What type of attack should Ann suspect?
questions.explanation: The attack described in this scenario has all the hallmarks of a denial-of-service attack. More specifically, Ann's organization is likely experiencing a DNS amplification attack where an attacker sends false requests to third-party DNS servers with a forged source IP address belonging to the targeted system. Because the attack uses UDP requests, there is no three-way handshake. The attack packets are carefully crafted to elicit a lengthy response from a short query. The purpose of these queries is to generate responses headed to the target system that are sufficiently large and numerous enough to overwhelm the targeted network or system.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Reconnaissance means probing or scanning to gather information about a target. It does not flood the network with large unsolicited responses that block legitimate users.

Incorrect. Malicious code such as viruses or worms runs on compromised hosts. Here the problem is a flood of oversized, unrequested inbound responses that exhausts bandwidth, which points to amplification rather than malware.

Incorrect. System penetration means gaining unauthorized access to a system. This scenario shows no access attempt. It shows a flood that makes the network unavailable, which is a denial-of-service symptom.

Correct. Large responses arriving from many sources to queries Ann's network never sent, and overwhelming it, describe a DoS attack, most likely DNS amplification. The attacker spoofs the victim's IP in short UDP queries to third-party DNS servers, which send large replies to the victim.

questions.stem:
Scenario:
Ann is a security professional for a midsize business and typically handles log analysis and security monitoring tasks for her organization. One of her roles is to monitor alerts originating from the organization's intrusion detection system. The system typically generates several dozen alerts each day, and many of those alerts turn out to be false alarms after her investigation. This morning, the intrusion detection system alerted because the network began to receive an unusually high volume of inbound traffic. Ann received this alert and began looking into the origin of the traffic.

Now that Ann understands that an attack has taken place that violates her organization's security policy, what term best describes what has occurred in Ann's organization?
questions.explanation: Now that Ann suspects an attack against her organization, she has sufficient evidence to declare a security incident. The attack underway seems to have undermined the availability of her network, meeting one of the criteria for a security incident. This is an escalation beyond a security event but does not reach the level of an intrusion because there is no evidence that the attacker has even attempted to gain access to systems on Ann's network. Security occurrence is not a term commonly used in incident handling.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The term "security occurrence" isn't commonly used in incident handling, so it doesn't fit this escalation.
Correct. A suspected attack that violates security policy and hurts network availability meets the criteria for a security incident, which is a step up from an event.
Incorrect. An event is any observable occurrence, such as the first alert. Once an attack that violates policy is confirmed, it has escalated past an event and into an incident.
Incorrect. An intrusion means an attacker gained, or tried to gain, access to systems. Here there's no evidence of any access attempt, only an inbound traffic flood.

questions.stem: Frank is seeking to introduce a hacker's laptop in court as evidence against the hacker. The laptop does contain logs that indicate the hacker committed the crime, but the court ruled that the search of the apartment that resulted in police finding the laptop was unconstitutional. What admissibility criteria prevents Frank from introducing the laptop as evidence?
questions.explanation: To be admissible, evidence must be relevant, material, and competent. The laptop in this case is clearly material because it contains logs related to the crime in question. It is also relevant because it provides evidence that ties the hacker to the crime. It is not competent because the evidence was not legally obtained.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Materiality asks whether the evidence relates to the matter at hand. The laptop holds logs about this specific crime, so it meets this test and materiality is not what blocks it.
Incorrect. Relevance asks whether the evidence helps prove or disprove a fact. The logs tie the hacker to the crime, so the laptop is relevant, and relevance does not block it.
Incorrect. The hearsay rule bars a witness from testifying about what someone else said outside court. It is not one of the three admissibility criteria and has nothing to do with an illegal search.
Correct. Competence requires that evidence be obtained legally. The laptop came from a search the court ruled unconstitutional, so it is not competent and cannot be admitted.

questions.stem: Gordon suspects that a hacker has penetrated a system belonging to his company. The system does not contain any regulated information, and Gordon wants to conduct an investigation on behalf of his company. He has permission from his supervisor to conduct the investigation. Which of the following statements is true?
options: Gordon is legally required to contact law enforcement before beginning the investigation.
Gordon may not conduct his own investigation.
Gordon's investigation may include examining the contents of hard disks, network traffic, and any other systems or information belonging to the company.
Gordon may ethically perform “hack back” activities after identifying the perpetrator.
questions.explanation: Gordon may conduct his investigation as he wants and use any information that is legally available to him, including information and systems belonging to his employer. There is no obligation to contact law enforcement. However, Gordon may not perform “hack back” activities because those may constitute violations of the law and/or ISC2 Code of Ethics.
optionNotes: Incorrect. No law requires a company to call law enforcement before it investigates its own systems, especially when no regulated data is involved. Bringing in police is the organization's choice.
Incorrect. Nothing stops Gordon from investigating. He has his supervisor's approval, and the systems belong to his own company.
Correct. Gordon can use any information that is legally available to him, which includes the disks, network traffic and other systems his employer owns.
Incorrect. Hacking back means attacking the perpetrator's systems. That may break the law and the ISC2 Code of Ethics, so Gordon can't do it ethically even once he knows who the attacker is.

questions.stem: Which one of the following tools provides an organization with the greatest level of protection against a software vendor going out of business?
questions.explanation: Software escrow agreements place a copy of the source code for a software package in the hands of an independent third party who will turn the code over to the customer if the vendor ceases business operations. Service-level agreements, mutual assistance agreements, and compliance agreements all lose some or all of their effectiveness if the vendor goes out of business.
optionNotes: Incorrect. An SLA sets performance expectations and penalties for the vendor. If the vendor goes out of business, nobody is left to meet those expectations or pay the penalties.

Correct. A software escrow agreement places the source code with an independent third party, who releases it to the customer if the vendor stops operating. This lets the customer keep maintaining the software.

Incorrect. A mutual assistance agreement is a promise between organizations to support each other, usually for disaster recovery facilities. It loses its value if the other party goes out of business and does not protect the customer's access to source code.
Incorrect. PCI DSS compliance is a contractual obligation to protect payment card data, enforced through merchant agreements. It has nothing to do with keeping software available if the vendor fails.

questions.stem: Fran is considering new human resources policies for her bank that will deter fraud. She plans to implement a mandatory vacation policy. What is typically considered the shortest effective length of a mandatory vacation?
questions.explanation: Most security professionals recommend at least one, and preferably two, weeks of vacation to deter fraud. The idea is that fraudulent schemes will be uncovered during the time that the employee is away and does not have the access required to perpetuate a cover-up.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Two days is too short. The employee could put off fraudulent transactions or cover-up work until they return, so the person filling in may not notice anything wrong. The book recommends at least one week.

Incorrect. Four days is still shorter than the one-week minimum. A short absence like this may not stop the employee from keeping up a cover-up, so the replacement is less likely to find irregularities.
Correct. Security professionals recommend at least one week, and preferably two. That is long enough for a fraud scheme to come to light while the employee has no access to keep covering it up.

Incorrect. A month would work, but it is far longer than the shortest effective length. The question asks for the minimum, and the guidance says one to two weeks is usually enough to detect irregularities.

questions.stem: Which of the following events would constitute a security incident? (Select all that apply.)
options: A successful attempt to access a file
A violation of a confidentiality policy
An unsuccessful attempt to remove information from a secured area
questions.explanation: Any attempt to undermine the security of an organization or violation of a security policy is a security incident. All of the events described meet this definition and should be treated as an incident, with one exception. A successful attempt to access a file is certainly a security event, but it is not a security incident unless it is established that the individual accessing the file was not authorized to do so.
optionNotes: Correct. An attempted intrusion counts as an attempt to undermine organizational security, so it is an incident even though it did not succeed.
Correct. A successful database intrusion undermines security and breaks policy. It is a clear security incident.
Correct. A malware infection undermines the security of the organization's systems, so it fits the definition of a security incident.
Incorrect. A successful file access is a security event. It only becomes an incident if the person accessing the file is shown to be unauthorized, and nothing in the question says that.
Correct. Violating a confidentiality policy is a security policy violation, and any policy violation is a security incident by definition.
Correct. Trying to remove information from a secured area is an attempt to undermine security. It is an incident even though it failed.

questions.stem: Amanda is configuring her organization's firewall to implement egress filtering. Which one of the following traffic types should be blocked by her organization's egress filtering policy? (Select all that apply.)
options: Traffic rapidly scanning many IP addresses on port 22
Traffic with a source address from an external network
Traffic with a destination address on an external network
questions.explanation: Egress filtering scans outbound traffic for potential security policy violations. This includes traffic that is likely malicious, such as an outbound SSH scan on port 22. It also includes traffic that appears to be part of an attack or misconfiguration, such as sending traffic to a broadcast destination address. Finally, it includes spoofed traffic generated by internal systems, which may bear a source address from an external network. The normal traffic that the firewall should expect to see is that bearing a destination address on an external network.
optionNotes: Correct. Outbound traffic that quickly scans many addresses on port 22 looks like an SSH scan coming from a compromised internal host. Egress filtering should block it.
Correct. Outbound traffic sent to a broadcast address suggests an attack (such as smurf-style amplification) or a misconfiguration, so the egress policy should drop it.
Correct. Outbound packets should carry internal source addresses. An external source address means an internal system is spoofing traffic, and egress filtering should block it.
Incorrect. Normal outbound traffic is addressed to external networks, so the firewall should expect to see these packets and allow them.

questions.stem: Allie is responsible for reviewing authentication logs on her organization's network. She does not have the time to review all logs, so she decides to choose only records where there have been four or more invalid authentication attempts. What technique is Allie using to reduce the size of the pool?
questions.explanation: The two main methods of choosing records from a large pool for further analysis are sampling and clipping. Sampling uses statistical techniques to choose a sample that is representative of the entire pool, while clipping uses threshold values to select those records that exceed a predefined threshold because they may be of most interest to analysts. In this case, Allie is only selecting records that exceed an invalid login threshold, making this an example of clipping. She is not using statistical techniques to select a subset of records, so this is not an example of sampling.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Sampling uses statistical techniques to pick a subset that represents the whole pool. Allie isn't choosing a representative subset. She's filtering on a threshold.
Incorrect. Random selection picks records by chance, so any record could be chosen. Allie keeps only records with four or more failed attempts, which is a deliberate threshold, not randomness.
Correct. Clipping uses a predefined threshold, here four or more invalid logins, to pull out only the records that exceed it, because those are likely to matter most to analysts.
Incorrect. Statistical analysis is the method behind sampling. Allie's selection uses no statistics, just a simple cutoff, so this doesn't describe how she reduced the pool.

questions.stem: You are performing an investigation into a potential bot infection on your network and want to perform a forensic analysis of the information that passed between different systems on your network and those on the Internet. You believe that the information was likely encrypted. You are beginning your investigation after the activity concluded. What would be the best and easiest way to obtain the source of this information?
questions.explanation: NetFlow data contains information on the source, destination, and size of all network communications and is routinely saved as a matter of normal activity. Packet capture data would provide relevant information, but it must be captured during the suspicious activity and cannot be re-created after the fact unless the organization is already conducting 100% packet capture, which is rare. Additionally, the use of encryption limits the effectiveness of packet capture. Intrusion detection system logs would not likely contain relevant information because the encrypted traffic would probably not match intrusion signatures. Centralized authentication records would not contain information about network traffic.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Packet captures have to be running while the activity happens. They can't be re-created afterward unless the organization already captures all traffic, which is rare, and encryption hides the payload anyway.

Correct. NetFlow records the source, destination and size of every network conversation and is saved routinely, so it's still available after the fact. Encryption doesn't matter because flow data never looks at the payload.
Incorrect. IDS logs record alerts when traffic matches a signature. Encrypted bot traffic probably wouldn't match any signature, so these logs likely hold little of value here.
Incorrect. Centralized authentication records track user logons, not traffic between systems, so they can't show where the network communications came from.

questions.stem: Which one of the following tools helps system administrators by providing a standard, secure template of configuration settings for operating systems and applications?
questions.explanation: Baseline configurations serve as the starting point for configuring secure systems and applications. They contain the security settings necessary to comply with an organization's security policy and may then be customized to meet the specific needs of an implementation. While security policies and guidelines may contain information needed to secure a system, they do not contain a set of configuration settings that may be applied to a system. The running configuration of a system is the set of currently applied settings, which may or may not be secure.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Guidelines are non-mandatory advice that may describe how to secure systems, but they are not a set of configuration settings that can be applied to a system.
Incorrect. A security policy sets high-level requirements that systems must meet. It does not contain the actual configuration settings to apply, although baselines are written to comply with it.
Correct. A baseline configuration is the standard, secure starting template of settings that satisfies the security policy. Administrators can then customize it for a specific implementation.
Incorrect. The running configuration is the set of settings currently applied to a system. It may or may not be secure, so it is not a standard template.

questions.stem: What type of disaster recovery test activates the alternate processing facility and uses it to conduct transactions but leaves the primary site up and running?
questions.explanation: During a parallel test, the team actually activates the disaster recovery site for testing, but the primary site remains operational. During a full interruption test, the team takes down the primary site and confirms that the disaster recovery site is capable of handling regular operations. The full interruption test is the most thorough test but also the most disruptive. The read-through is the least disruptive type of disaster recovery test. During a read-through, team members each review the contents of their disaster recovery checklists on their own and suggest any necessary changes. During a tabletop exercise, team members come together and work through a specific scenario without making any changes to information systems.
optionNotes: Incorrect. A full interruption test shuts down the primary site and moves operations to the DR site. The question says the primary site stays up, so this isn't it. It's the most thorough test and also the most disruptive.
Correct. A parallel test activates the DR site and runs transactions there while the primary site keeps operating, so you can check the alternate site without disrupting the business.
Incorrect. A read-through is the least disruptive test. Each team member reviews their DR checklist on their own and suggests changes. No facility gets activated.
Incorrect. In a tabletop exercise the team meets to walk through a scenario together. No changes are made to information systems, and the alternate site isn't activated or used for transactions.

questions.stem: During which phase of the incident response process would an analyst receive an intrusion detection system alert and verify its accuracy?
questions.explanation: Both the receipt of alerts and the verification of their accuracy occur during the Detection phase of the incident response process.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Response is the phase that comes after an alert has been confirmed as an incident. That's when the team is activated to handle it, so it doesn't cover receiving and checking the alert.
Incorrect. Mitigation is about containing a confirmed incident so it can't spread or cause more damage. It happens after detection and validation, not when the alert first arrives.
Correct. The Detection phase is where alerts (such as IDS alerts) come in and analysts check whether they are true positives before treating them as incidents.
Incorrect. Reporting means notifying management, regulators or others about an incident that has been confirmed. It comes after detection and doesn't include checking whether alerts are accurate.

questions.stem: Kevin is developing a continuous security monitoring strategy for his organization. Which one of the following is not normally used when determining assessment and monitoring frequency?
questions.explanation: According to NIST SP 800-137, organizations should use the following factors to determine assessment and monitoring frequency: security control volatility, system categorizations/impact levels, security controls or specific assessment objects providing critical functions, security controls with identified weaknesses, organizational risk tolerance, threat information, vulnerability information, risk assessment results, the output of monitoring strategy reviews, and reporting requirements.
optionNotes: Incorrect. NIST SP 800-137 lists threat information as a factor for setting monitoring frequency. New or rising threats can justify assessing the affected controls more often.
Incorrect. SP 800-137 explicitly lists system categorization/impact level. Higher-impact systems usually get assessed and monitored more frequently.

Correct. Operational burden is not one of the SP 800-137 frequency factors. Frequency should follow risk, meaning volatility, criticality, weaknesses, threats, vulnerabilities and risk tolerance, not how inconvenient a control is to run.
Incorrect. SP 800-137 names organizational risk tolerance as a factor. Organizations with low tolerance for risk need to assess and monitor more often.

questions.stem: Hunter is reviewing his organization's monitoring strategy and identifying new technologies that they might deploy. His assessment reveals that the firm is not doing enough to monitor employee activity on endpoint devices. Which one of the following technologies would best meet his needs?
questions.explanation: All of these technologies have the potential to monitor user behavior on endpoint devices. The key to answering this question correctly is realizing the emphasis on the user. Intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDSs/IPSs) focus on network and host behavior. Endpoint detection and response (EDR) systems focus on endpoint devices. User and entity behavior analytics (UEBA) solutions focus on the user and, therefore, would be the best way to meet Hunter's requirement.
optionNotes: Incorrect. EDR watches endpoint devices for unusual device behavior and supports response, but its focus is the endpoint itself rather than profiling and analyzing individual user activity.
Incorrect. An IPS monitors network or host traffic and blocks malicious activity. It looks at network and host behavior, not the activity patterns of individual employees.
Incorrect. An IDS detects and alerts on suspicious network or host behavior. Like an IPS, it isn't built to profile and monitor what individual users do.
Correct. UEBA builds behavior profiles for each user and flags deviations from them. Its focus on the user makes it the best fit for monitoring employee activity on endpoints.

questions.stem: Bruce is seeing quite a bit of suspicious activity on his network. After consulting records in his SIEM, it appears that an outside entity is attempting to connect to all of his systems using a TCP connection on port 22. What type of scanning is the outsider likely engaging in?
questions.explanation: SSH uses TCP port 22, so this attack is likely an attempt to scan for open or weakly secured SSH servers. FTP uses ports 20 and 21. Telnet uses port 23, and HTTP uses port 80.
optionNotes: Incorrect. FTP runs on TCP ports 20 (data) and 21 (control), not 22. An FTP scan would show probes to those ports.
Incorrect. Telnet uses TCP port 23. It is the insecure remote-access protocol that SSH replaced, but traffic to port 22 points to SSH, not Telnet.
Correct. SSH listens on TCP port 22, so connection attempts to port 22 across every host look like a sweep for open or weakly secured SSH servers.
Incorrect. HTTP uses TCP port 80, and HTTPS uses 443. An HTTP scan would target web ports, not port 22.

questions.stem: Dylan believes that a database server in his environment was compromised using a SQL injection attack. Which one of the following actions would Dylan most likely take during the remediation phase of the attack?
options: Adding input validation to a web application
questions.explanation: Remediation activities seek to address the issue that caused the incident. In this case, that was a web application that was open to SQL injection attack. Adding input validation seeks to remediate this vulnerability. Rebuilding the database is a recovery action, while reviewing logs is done as part of the detection and response effort.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Rebuilding the database from backups puts the system back into service. That is a recovery step, not remediation, and it leaves the SQL injection flaw still exploitable.
Correct. Remediation fixes the root cause of the incident. Here the cause was a web application open to SQL injection, so adding input validation closes that vulnerability.
Incorrect. Firewall logs are reviewed during detection and response, to spot and scope the attack. Reviewing them doesn't fix the underlying vulnerability.
Incorrect. Reviewing database logs is part of detection and response, used to confirm and investigate the compromise. It doesn't remediate the injection flaw.

questions.stem: Roger recently accepted a new position as a security professional at a company that runs its entire IT infrastructure within an IaaS environment. Which one of the following would most likely be the responsibility of Roger's firm?
questions.explanation: In an infrastructure-as-a-service environment, the vendor is responsible for hardware- and network-related responsibilities. These include configuring network firewalls, maintaining the hypervisor, and managing physical equipment. The customer retains responsibility for patching operating systems on its virtual machine instances.
optionNotes: Incorrect. The book places network firewall configuration with the IaaS vendor, which owns the network side of the infrastructure. So it isn't the customer's job here.
Incorrect. The book says the IaaS provider maintains the hypervisor that its virtual machines run on. The customer can't reach the hypervisor layer to update it.
Correct. In IaaS, the customer runs its own virtual machine instances, including the guest operating systems. That makes OS patching the customer's job.
Incorrect. Wiping drives is part of managing physical equipment, which the book assigns to the IaaS vendor. The customer never has physical access to the storage media.

questions.stem: What technique can application developers use to test applications in an isolated virtualized environment before allowing them on a production network?
questions.explanation: Sandboxing is a technique where application developers (or the recipients of an untrusted application) may test the code in a virtualized environment that is isolated from production systems. White-box testing, black-box testing, and penetration testing are all common software testing techniques but do not require the use of an isolated system.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Penetration testing simulates attacks to find exploitable weaknesses. It's a testing technique, but it doesn't require running code in an isolated virtualized environment.
Correct. Sandboxing runs untrusted or new code in a virtualized environment that is isolated from production systems, so it can be tested safely before deployment.
Incorrect. White-box testing means testing with full knowledge of the source code and internal logic. It's about how much the tester knows, not about isolating the code in a virtual environment.
Incorrect. Black-box testing checks the application from the outside, with no knowledge of its internals. It's a common technique, but it doesn't involve an isolated virtualized system.

questions.stem: Gina is the firewall administrator for a small business and recently installed a new firewall. After seeing signs of unusually heavy network traffic, she checked the intrusion detection system, which reported that a SYN flood attack was underway. What firewall configuration change can Gina make to most effectively prevent this attack?
options: Enable SYN-ACK spoofing at the firewall.
questions.explanation: While it may not immediately seem like the obvious answer, many firewalls have a built-in anti–SYN flood defense that responds to SYNs on behalf of protected systems. Once the remote system proves to be a legitimate connection by continuing the three-way handshake, the rest of the TCP session is passed through. If the connection proves to be an attack, the firewall handles the additional load using appropriate mitigation techniques. Blocking SYNs from known or unknown IP addresses is likely to cause issues with systems that should be able to connect, and turning off TCP will break most modern network services!
optionNotes: Incorrect. SYN floods usually come from spoofed, changing source addresses. Blocking SYNs from known IPs would mostly cut off legitimate systems that need to connect, and it wouldn't reliably stop the attack.
Incorrect. A business has to accept connections from unknown clients. Blocking their SYNs would cut off legitimate users, and the flood's spoofed sources would still change from packet to packet.

Correct. The firewall's anti-SYN-flood feature answers SYNs for the protected hosts and passes a session through only after the client completes the three-way handshake. The firewall absorbs and mitigates the bogus half-open connections.
Incorrect. Turning off TCP would break most modern network services. That causes the very denial of service the attacker wants, so it isn't mitigation.

questions.stem: Nancy is leading an effort to modernize her organization's antimalware protection and would like to add endpoint detection and response (EDR) capabilities. Which of the following actions are normally supported by EDR systems? (Select all that apply.)
options: Analyzing endpoint memory, filesystem, and network activity for signs of malicious activity
Automatically isolating possible malicious activity to contain the potential damage
questions.explanation: EDR platforms do not conduct simulated phishing campaigns. The most common features of EDR systems are analyzing endpoint memory, filesystem, and network activity for signs of malicious activity; isolating possible malicious activity to contain the potential damage; integrating with threat intelligence sources; and integrating with other incident response mechanisms.
optionNotes: Correct. EDR's core function is continuously monitoring endpoint memory, filesystem, and network activity to spot signs of malicious behavior that signature-based antivirus can miss.
Correct. EDR platforms can automatically isolate suspicious processes or endpoints, which contains the potential damage while responders investigate.
Incorrect. Simulated phishing campaigns are part of security awareness training and are run with phishing-simulation tools. EDR doesn't do this; it monitors endpoints and responds to threats.
Correct. EDR systems commonly pull in threat intelligence feeds so they can match endpoint activity against known indicators of compromise. They also integrate with other incident response tools.

questions.stem: Alan is assessing the potential for using machine learning and artificial intelligence in his cybersecurity program. Which of the following activities is most likely to benefit from this technology?
questions.explanation: While any cybersecurity activity has the potential to benefit from machine learning and artificial intelligence capabilities, this technology really shines when used for pattern detection and anomaly detection problems. This is the type of activity performed by an intrusion detection system, and, therefore, this system would benefit the most from the use of ML/AI technology.
optionNotes: Correct. ML/AI does best at finding patterns and anomalies, and that is the core job of an intrusion detection system, especially a behavior-based one that compares activity to a baseline of normal behavior.

Incorrect. Account provisioning is a rules-driven administrative workflow (create accounts, assign rights). It can be automated without any pattern or anomaly detection, so ML/AI adds little compared with an IDS.

Incorrect. Changing firewall rules is a deliberate configuration task, normally handled through change management. It isn't a pattern-recognition problem, so it gains less from ML/AI than anomaly-based intrusion detection does.
Incorrect. Media sanitization means physically or logically destroying data by clearing, purging, or destroying the media. It needs no pattern analysis, so ML/AI offers essentially no benefit.

questions.stem: Timber Industries recently had a dispute with a customer. During a meeting with his account representative, the customer stood up and declared, “There is no other solution. We will have to take this matter to court.” He then left the room. When does Timber Industries have an obligation to begin preserving evidence?
options: Upon receipt of a notice of litigation from opposing attorneys
Upon receipt of a court order
questions.explanation: Companies have an obligation to preserve evidence whenever they believe that the threat of litigation is imminent. The statement made by this customer that “we will have to take this matter to court” is a clear threat of litigation and should trigger the preservation of any related documents and records.
optionNotes: Correct. The duty to preserve evidence starts as soon as litigation is reasonably anticipated. The customer saying "we will have to take this matter to court" is a clear threat, so preservation should start right away.
Incorrect. Waiting for a formal notice from opposing attorneys is too late. The duty to preserve starts when litigation becomes imminent, and the customer's spoken threat already meets that bar.

Incorrect. A subpoena is a formal demand for evidence that usually comes after litigation is underway. Destroying records before it arrives, once litigation was already foreseeable, could count as spoliation.
Incorrect. A court order is the latest trigger listed. The preservation obligation comes long before a court is involved, starting once litigation is reasonably anticipated.

questions.stem: Candace is designing a backup strategy for her organization's file server. She would like to perform a backup every weekday that has the smallest possible storage footprint. What type of backup should she perform?
questions.explanation: Incremental backups provide the option that includes the smallest amount of data. In this case, that would be only the data modified since the most recent incremental backup. A differential backup would back up all data modified since the last full backup, which would be a substantial amount. The full backup would include all information on the server. Transaction log backups are specifically designed to support database servers and would not be effective on a file server.
optionNotes: Correct. Incremental backups capture only data changed since the most recent backup (full or incremental), which gives each daily backup the smallest storage footprint.
Incorrect. A full backup copies all data on the server every time, so it has the largest storage footprint of the options.
Incorrect. A differential backup copies everything changed since the last full backup. Each day it grows larger, so it is bigger than an incremental backup.
Incorrect. Transaction log backups are made for database servers. They would not be effective for backing up a file server.

questions.stem: Darcy is a computer security specialist who is assisting with the prosecution of a hacker. The prosecutor requests that Darcy give testimony in court about whether, in her opinion, the logs and other records in a case are indicative of a hacking attempt. What type of evidence is Darcy being asked to provide?
questions.explanation: Expert opinion evidence allows individuals to offer their opinion based upon the facts in evidence and their personal knowledge. Expert opinion evidence may be offered only if the court accepts the witness as an expert in a particular field. Direct evidence is when witnesses testify about their direct observations. Real evidence consists of tangible items brought into court as evidence. Documentary evidence consists of written records used as evidence in court.
optionNotes: Correct. Darcy is giving her opinion on what the logs mean, based on the facts in evidence and her own specialist knowledge. That is expert opinion testimony, and the court must first accept her as an expert in the field.
Incorrect. Direct evidence is a witness describing what they personally saw or heard. Darcy is interpreting records, not reporting her own first-hand observations of the attack.
Incorrect. Real evidence means physical objects brought into court, such as a seized hard drive. Darcy's testimony is spoken opinion, not a physical item.
Incorrect. Documentary evidence is written records, like the logs themselves. Darcy is asked to interpret those records, not to present them as evidence.

questions.stem: Which one of the following techniques is not commonly used to remove unwanted remnant data from magnetic tapes?
questions.explanation: The standard methods for clearing magnetic tapes, according to the NIST Guidelines for Media Sanitization, are overwriting the tape with nonsensitive data, degaussing, and physical destruction via shredding. Reformatting a tape does not remove remnant data.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Physical destruction, such as shredding, is one of the standard NIST sanitization methods for magnetic tape. It is commonly used, so it is not the answer.
Incorrect. Degaussing removes data by scrambling the magnetic domains on the tape. NIST lists it as a standard tape sanitization method, so it is not the answer.
Incorrect. Overwriting the tape with nonsensitive data is a standard NIST clearing method for magnetic tape. It is commonly used, so it is not the answer.
Correct. Reformatting only rewrites the tape's structure and leaves the remnant data recoverable. It is not a NIST tape sanitization method.

questions.stem: Sally is building a new server for use in her environment and plans to implement RAID level 1 as a storage availability control. What is the minimum number of physical hard disks that she needs to implement this approach?
questions.explanation: RAID level 1, also known as disk mirroring, uses a minimum of two disks that contain identical information. If one disk fails, the other contains the data needed for the system to continue operation.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Mirroring copies data to a second disk, so it can't be done with one disk. A single drive has no redundancy and leaves a single point of failure.
Correct. RAID 1 (disk mirroring) needs at least two disks holding identical data. If one fails, the other keeps the system running.
Incorrect. Three disks is the minimum for RAID 5 (striping with distributed parity), not RAID 1. Mirroring needs only two.
Incorrect. No common RAID level has a minimum of five disks. RAID 6 needs four, RAID 5 needs three, and RAID 1 mirroring needs only two.

questions.stem: Jerome is conducting a forensic investigation and is reviewing database server logs to investigate query contents for evidence of SQL injection attacks. What type of analysis is he performing?
questions.explanation: The analysis of application logs is one of the core tasks of software analysis. This is the correct answer because SQL injection attacks are application attacks.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Hardware analysis looks at physical devices such as memory chips, embedded systems, and components. Reviewing database query logs for SQL injection doesn't involve examining hardware.
Correct. Reviewing application logs is a core task of software analysis, and SQL injection is an attack on the application. So examining database server query logs counts as software analysis.
Incorrect. Network analysis looks at traffic captures, flow data, and network device logs. Jerome is reviewing database query contents in server logs, not network traffic.

Incorrect. Media analysis means finding and extracting information from storage media, such as hard drive images and slack space. Jerome is reviewing application log contents, not recovering data from media.

questions.stem: Quigley Computing regularly ships tapes of backup data across the country to a secondary facility. These tapes contain confidential information. What is the most important security control that Quigley can use to protect these tapes?
questions.explanation: Quigley may choose to use any or all of these security controls, but data encryption is, by far, the most important control. It protects the confidentiality of data stored on the tapes, which are most vulnerable to theft while in transit between two secure locations.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Locked containers are a physical deterrent that can help, but if the container is stolen or forced open, the data is exposed. Encryption keeps the data confidential even after the tapes are lost.
Incorrect. Private couriers lower the risk of mishandling, but tapes can still be lost or stolen in transit. Couriers don't protect the data itself the way encryption does.
Correct. Encryption protects the confidentiality of the data on the tapes even if they are stolen in transit between the two secure sites, when they are most vulnerable.
Incorrect. Media rotation is a backup-management practice (e.g., grandfather-father-son) for retention and media wear. It does nothing to protect confidentiality during shipment.

questions.stem: Carolyn is concerned that users on her network may be storing sensitive information, such as Social Security numbers, on their hard drives without proper authorization or security controls. What third-party security service can she implement to best detect this activity?
questions.explanation: Data loss prevention (DLP) systems may identify sensitive information stored on endpoint systems or in transit over a network. This is their primary purpose. DLP systems are commonly available as a third-party managed service offering. Intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDSs/IPSs) may be used to identify some sensitive information using signatures built for that purpose, but this is not the primary role of those tools, and they would not be as effective as DLP systems at this task. TLS is a network encryption protocol that may be used to protect sensitive information, but it does not have any ability to identify sensitive information.
optionNotes: Incorrect. An IDS looks for malicious activity. Custom signatures can flag some sensitive data, but that isn't its main job, so it won't find SSNs sitting on endpoint drives as well as DLP does.

Incorrect. An IPS blocks attacks in line with traffic. Like an IDS, it can match some sensitive data with signatures, but finding stored sensitive data isn't its purpose, so it is less effective here than DLP.

Correct. The main purpose of DLP is to find sensitive information, such as SSNs, whether it is stored on endpoints or moving across the network. DLP is also commonly offered as a third-party managed service.
Incorrect. TLS is a network encryption protocol. It can protect sensitive data in transit, but it has no way to detect or identify sensitive data stored on hard drives.

questions.stem: Gavin is the disaster recovery team leader for his organization, which is currently in the response phase of an incident that has severe customer impact. Gavin just received a phone call from a reporter asking for details on the root cause and an estimated recovery time. Gavin has this information at his fingertips. What should he do?
options: Provide the information to the reporter.
Request a few minutes to gather the information and return the call.
Refer the matter to the public relations department.
questions.explanation: Disaster recovery teams should always refer media inquiries to the public relations team to ensure a coordinated, consistent response. They should not attempt to answer questions themselves.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Even though Gavin has the details, DR team members shouldn't answer media questions themselves. Doing so goes around the coordinated, consistent public message that PR is responsible for managing.
Incorrect. Calling the reporter back with the details is still the DR team talking to the media directly. Waiting a few minutes doesn't fix that; the inquiry belongs with public relations.
Correct. DR teams should always send media inquiries to the public relations team so the organization gives one coordinated, consistent response.
Incorrect. A flat refusal leaves the request unhandled and can hurt the organization's reputation. The right move is to pass the reporter to PR, who can respond properly.

questions.stem: Pauline is reviewing her organization's emergency management plans. What should be the highest priority when creating these plans?
questions.explanation: All of these considerations are important when developing an emergency management plan. However, the safety of human life should always be the overwhelming priority, above all other considerations.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Protecting mission-critical data matters in emergency planning, but data can be restored from backups. It always ranks below the safety of human life.
Incorrect. Keeping operational systems running is a business continuity and recovery goal. It is secondary to protecting people during an emergency.
Incorrect. Evidence collection matters for incident response and investigations. It is never a higher priority than the safety of human life in an emergency.
Correct. Human safety is always the top priority, above data, systems and evidence. Emergency management plans exist mainly to address personnel safety and security after a disaster.

questions.stem: Barry is the CIO of an organization that recently suffered a serious operational issue that required activation of the disaster recovery plan. He would like to conduct a lessons learned session to review the incident. Who would be the best facilitator for this session?
questions.explanation: Barry should recruit an independent moderator to facilitate the session. Having a moderator who was not directly involved in the effort encourages honest and open feedback. While it is not necessary to use an external consultant, they may easily fill this role. While it is also possible to find a qualified internal employee to fill this position, it should not be someone who was involved in the incident response effort or has a major stake in the plan, such as Barry, the CISO, or the DR team leader.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Barry runs IT and has a major stake in the DR plan and how the response went. If he facilitates, participants may hold back honest criticism, so he shouldn't moderate.
Incorrect. The CISO was likely involved in the response and has a stake in the plan. That conflict of interest gets in the way of the open, honest feedback the session needs.
Incorrect. The DR team leader directed the recovery effort being reviewed, so they aren't independent. Team members may not want to criticize their own leader's decisions.

Correct. An external consultant is an independent moderator who wasn't involved in the incident, which encourages candid feedback. A qualified uninvolved insider could also do this, but the consultant fits the role easily.

questions.stem: Brent is reviewing the controls that will protect his organization in the event of a sustained period of power loss. Which one of the following solutions would best meet his needs?
questions.explanation: Generators are capable of providing backup power for a sustained period of time in the event of a power loss, but they take time to activate. Uninterruptible power supplies (UPSs) provide immediate, battery-driven power for a short period of time to cover momentary losses of power, which would not cover a sustained period of power loss. RAID and redundant servers are high-availability controls but do not cover power loss scenarios.
optionNotes: Incorrect. Redundant servers are a high-availability control against server failure. If the whole facility loses power, the redundant servers go down too, so they don't solve a power problem.
Incorrect. A UPS gives immediate battery power, but only for a short time. It covers momentary outages or bridges the gap until a generator starts, not a sustained power loss.
Correct. A generator can supply backup power for a long period during an outage. It takes time to start, but it is the right control for a sustained power loss.
Incorrect. RAID protects data availability when a disk fails. It does nothing to keep systems running when power is lost.

questions.stem:
Match each of the numbered terms with its correct lettered definition:
Terms:
1. Honeypot
2. Honeynet
3. Pseudo-flaw
4. Darknet

(Arrange the options in the order of the numbered items 1–4.)
options: An intentionally designed vulnerability used to lure in an attacker
A network set up with intentional vulnerabilities
A system set up with intentional vulnerabilities
A monitored network without any hosts
questions.explanation:
The terms match with the definitions as follows:
1. Honeypot: C. A system set up with intentional vulnerabilities
2. Honeynet: B. A network set up with intentional vulnerabilities
3. Pseudo-flaw: A. An intentionally designed vulnerability used to lure in an attacker
4. Darknet: D. A monitored network without any hosts
optionNotes: Goes with item 3, pseudo-flaw. It's one deliberately planted vulnerability, such as a fake bug in code or a system, used to lure an attacker. It is not a whole system or network.
Goes with item 2, honeynet. A honeynet is a whole network of decoy systems with deliberate vulnerabilities, not just one host.
Goes with item 1, honeypot. A honeypot is a single decoy system left deliberately vulnerable to attract attackers and watch what they do.

Goes with item 4, darknet. A darknet is unused address space that is monitored but has no hosts on it, so any traffic it receives is suspicious. Unlike a honeypot or honeynet, it has no deliberate vulnerabilities.

questions.stem:
Match each of the numbered types of recovery capabilities to their correct lettered definition:
Terms:
1. Hot site
2. Cold site
3. Warm site
4. Service bureau

(Arrange the options in the order of the numbered items 1–4.)
options: An organization that can provide on-site or off-site IT services in the event of a disaster
A site with dedicated storage and real-time data replication, often with shared equipment that allows restoration of service in a very short time
A site that relies on shared storage and backups for recovery
A rented space with power, cooling, and connectivity that can accept equipment as part of a recovery effort
questions.explanation:
The terms match with the definitions as follows:
1. Hot site: B. A site with dedicated storage and real-time data replication, often with shared equipment that allows restoration of service in a very short time
2. Cold site: D. A rented space with power, cooling, and connectivity that can accept equipment as part of a recovery effort
3. Warm site: C. A site that relies on shared storage and backups for recovery
4. Service bureau: A. An organization that can provide on-site or off-site IT services in the event of a disaster
optionNotes: Goes with item 4, service bureau. A service bureau is an outside organization contracted to supply IT services on-site or off-site after a disaster. It isn't a facility type that the organization occupies itself.
Goes with item 1, hot site. Dedicated storage and real-time data replication allow service to be restored in a very short time, which is what defines a hot site.
Goes with item 3, warm site. A warm site relies on shared storage and on restoring from backups, so recovery is slower than at a hot site but faster than at a cold site.
Goes with item 2, cold site. A cold site is rented space with only power, cooling and connectivity. Equipment has to be brought in during recovery, so restoration takes the longest.
